name: Reality Fracture
credit: Archetypes and signpost cards from Wizards of the Coast's Reality Fracture Prerelease Guide. Players' notes, rankings and extra key cards from Draftsim's draft guide (October 2026) and MTG Arena Zone's archetype guide, reworded.
about: The ally-color decks are the five colleges of Hexhaven; the enemy-color decks follow the set's big characters. Players found the games run long and turn on card advantage and bombs. Fixing is better than usual, so splashing is easy and pays off in both draft and sealed. Empower Jace and your total resources matter, and there is little graveyard hate.

src.t: Reality Fracture Prerelease Guide (Wizards of the Coast)
FRA Limited archetypes and example decks (MTG Arena Zone)

list.d: Surveil and scry to line up your next draws, then cash those choices in with cards that reward looking ahead. Keeps creatures attacking.
list.p: The top pair a week in. Keep a low-loyalty Jace token alive for its surveil, and play fragile cards in a careful order.

list.d: Fill your graveyard to seven or more cards with self-mill and cheap spells, then turn on the threshold payoffs. Snowballs once the graveyard is stocked.
list.p: Build around the graveyard payoffs; the format has little graveyard hate. Use Paradox Shaper to recycle spells so you never mill yourself out.

list.d: Removal and direct damage that also hit the opponent, with cards that get stronger whenever you deal noncombat damage. Can finish a game after the board clogs.
list.p: Attacking is often worth less here than you would think: ping with Vicious Verse and draw cards while your own life total is safe.

list.d: Heartwood tokens, a red-green mana rock, put big creatures on the table early.
list.p: Cheap blockers and removal buy the turns your Heartwood tokens need to set up the big threats.

list.d: Gain life in small bursts and turn it into +1/+1 counters, then keep those counters on the board.
list.p: Repeatable life gain beats one-off gains, and the Seed Suture creatures make the triggers reliable. One or two Medic's Kitesail make removal-heavy opponents spend it on your creatures.

list.d: Chip in with small creatures, then profit when they die or are sacrificed, turning each one into several resources.
list.p: Ranked last. Only lean into sacrifice if the enablers come to you; otherwise play your best white and black cards and splash removal and bombs.

list.d: A controlling spells deck: cheap instants and sorceries trigger your noncreature-spell payoffs while keeping the other side of the board clear.
list.p: Play it as tempo-control: keep cantrips and cheap interaction flowing so a prowess trigger happens every turn.

list.d: A stampede of creatures that each bring value: when they are cast, when they die and from the graveyard.
list.p: Treat it as a good-stuff deck that splashes the best cards you see. Take, and splash, every Recursive Recruitment.

list.d: Aggressive: grow your creatures with +1/+1 counters, make Cadet tokens and pump the team before the opponent stabilizes.
list.p: Good cards and a good curve matter more than counter synergies. Lean on cheap removal and combat tricks.

list.d: Empower Jace again and again and draw value from the planeswalker token over the whole game.
list.p: Plan your turns around empowering Jace. Don't surveil cards away unless you need lands or spells.
